sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Portable Phased-Array Medical Diagnostic Scanners

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary national system); corporate law governed principally by Law 32 of 1927, which follows a hybrid U.S.-style corporation statute adapted to Panamanian civil law procedure; no sub-state commercial code variations.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: People's Republic of China–Panama Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed December 2018)
Panama–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 31 October 2012; investment chapter)
Panama–Canada Free Trade Agreement (in force 1 April 2013; investment chapter)
Panama–United Kingdom Partnership and Investment Agreement (in force 2021)
Panama–Peru Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 1 May 2012; investment chapter)
Panama–Chile Free Trade Agreement (in force 2008; investment chapter)
Treaty-network note: Panama's tax treaty network is largely TIEA-based; the Barbados DTA is the principal double-tax convention in force.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT preventive regime and UBO register), as amended by Law 129 of 2020; Executive Decree 202 of 21 December 2016; Resolución SSNF No. 07-2020 (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales); Law 41 of 2000 and Law 2 of 2011 (Unidad de Análisis Financiero and organic AML framework); Law 42 of 2007 (customer due diligence obligations).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin (e.g., Hong Kong or PRC notarial authority)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Panama is a contracting state to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of certificate of incorporation and bylaws of the immediate corporate shareholder (if any)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of the passport of each UBO and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of origin based on the passport issued by the relevant national authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter for each UBO or contributing corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization or Hague Apostille as accepted by the Panamanian bank's compliance department

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing of the ultimate corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the shareholder jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn Spanish translation of the apostilled corporate and identity documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panamanian licensed court interpreter (Traductor Público Autorizado)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of the interpreter's signature before a Panamanian notary; translation must be attached to the apostilled original

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, authorized signatories, and material counterparties against the OFAC SDN and sectoral lists, the UN Security Council consolidated list and UNSCR 1373 designations, the EU consolidated sanctions list, the UK HM Treasury consolidated list, and domestic Panamanian designations issued by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero; enhanced due diligence is mandatory for foreign, domestic, and international-organization PEPs, including documented source of wealth and source of funds; suspicious transaction reports must be filed with the UAF under Law 42 of 2007, Law 23 of 2015, and SSNF regulations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Sede Electrónica (online corporate name search and reservation module at https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa/sede-electronica), submitted exclusively through a licensed Panamanian attorney.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Latin script; Spanish is the official inscription language, but foreign-sounding names are admitted if phonetically and orthographically adapted to Spanish usage; the corporate name must end with 'Sociedad Anónima' or the abbreviation 'S.A.' under Law 32 of 1927; the Public Registry rejects identical, confusingly similar, or impermissible names.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Nacional / República de Panamá / Panamá (implying official state character)
Universidad / Museo / Policía / Municipal (requiring ministerial or state authorization)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is valid for thirty (30) calendar days and is not extendable; upon rejection, the applicant may file a 'recurso de reposición' (reconsideration) with the Director General of the Public Registry within five (5) business days of notification, followed by a 'recurso de apelación' to the superior registry instance under Law 38 of 2000, and ultimately a 'demanda contencioso-administrativa' before the Sala Tercera of the Supreme Court; in parallel, the applicant may immediately resubmit a materially different alternative name for a new clearance cycle; submitting two alternative names in the initial filing reduces rejection risk.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible: a Panama S.A. may use the registered agent's physical address as its registered office without leasing separate premises, provided all commercial substance, manufacturing, warehousing, and staffing occur outside Panamanian territory; if the S.A. conducts manufacturing, storage, or employment within Panama, a physical establishment, municipal 'Aviso de Operación', and DGI registration are mandatory; for an export-oriented low-risk medical imaging trading and consignment structure, a virtual office is compliant.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-Moderate: estimated 15–25% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 24 months, mainly triggered by inconsistent UBO filings, nominee officer usage, sanctions or PEP hits, and EU/FATF monitoring of Panamanian corporate transparency; a plain-vanilla S.A. with no local employees and clean UBO records faces approximately 10% inspection likelihood.

Attorney fees for drafting articles of incorporation, internal bylaws, and first legal opinion

Initial UBO filing (Beneficiario Final) with the Superintendency of Non-Financial Subjects

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market compliance fee for low-risk medical device exporter

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 32 de 26 de febrero de 1927 (Ley General de Sociedades), as amended by Ley No. 5 de 2013 and Ley No. 62 de 2016; Articles 1-17 (formation, capital, and registration), Article 11 (directors' duties), and Article 31 (registered office and resident agent); Executive Decree 416/2013 on private-document incorporations by licensed attorneys.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección Mercantil (Mercantile Section of the National Public Registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Pacto Social y Estatutos / Escritura Constitutiva de Sociedad Anónima (private instrument subscribed before a licensed attorney and inscribed in the Mercantile Register)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed capital of B/.10,000 (USD 10,000 at par) under Ley 32 de 1927, Article 5; no paid-up capital or escrow account is required at formation, but paid-in capital must be demonstrable if the S.A. conducts business within Panamanian territory.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Board of Directors accepts the subscription of the corporation's authorized share capital as issued to the founding subscriber, acknowledges the subscribed funds, and directs that the issued shares be entered in the share register. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the corporation in Panama shall be maintained at the address of the resident agent, and such office is adopted as the statutory domicile for service of process. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed President, [Name] is appointed Secretary, and [Name] is appointed Treasurer, each to serve until the next annual meeting or until successors are elected and qualified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Reservation (Certificado de Búsqueda de Nombre)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección Mercantil, through the online registration system or the physical window via a licensed attorney.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the Panamanian resident agent (abogado idóneo) to run a name search for S.A. denominations on the Public Registry's corporate index. The registry confirms that the proposed denomination is distinguishable from existing registered societies; the attorney then reserves the selected name (valid for 15-30 days) and obtains the search certificate to attach to the incorporation instrument.
required_dossiers: Carta de Instrucciones signed by the intended shareholder or settlor
Copy of the passport or Panamanian ID (DUI) and proof of address of the shareholder and officers
Proposed corporate denomination (1-3 alternative names)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is denied, obtain the registry's denial note, submit alternative denominations, or file a reconsideration petition (recurso de reconsideración) within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Articles of Incorporation (Pacto Social y Estatutos)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Panamanian attorney acting as incorporator; execution as a private document under Ley 32 de 1927 as reformed by Ley 5 de 2013.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The attorney drafts the articles of incorporation containing the corporate purpose (manufacture, assembly, distribution, and export of portable medical diagnostic imaging systems, including color Doppler ultrasound consoles), the minimum B/.10,000 subscribed capital, share classes, board provisions, the resident agent clause, and the officers' structure. The incorporator signs the instrument before the attorney; notarization is obtained if required by a counterparty. Attach the name search certificate and instruction letters.
required_dossiers: Final draft of Pacto Social y Estatutos in Spanish
Certificado de Búsqueda de Nombre
Carta de Instrucciones executed by the beneficial owner
Passport or ID copies of the incorporator, directors, and officers
Resident agent acceptance letter (Carta de Aceptación del Agente Residente)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Revise any statutory deficiencies flagged by counsel, re-execute the corrected instrument, and re-issue the resident agent acceptance letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the Corporation in the Mercantile Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección Mercantil; online presentation through the electronic registration system or in-person filing window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed incorporation instrument with the Mercantile Section together with proof of payment of the registry tariff (B/.200 for the first 10 pages plus additional page charges). The registry verifies formal compliance with Ley 32 de 1927, assigns an entry number, and inscribes the S.A. in the Mercantile Register. Upon approval, obtain the certificate of inscription or electronic acknowledgment.
required_dossiers: Original signed Pacto Social y Estatutos
Proof of payment of registry fees (recibo de caja or legal tariff receipt)
Certificate of name search (filed with the instrument)
Power of attorney or direct filing authorization for the presenting attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a rejection note (nota de devolución) is issued, appeal to the Director General of the Registro Público within 5 business days, cure the cited formal defect, and resubmit within the 30-day rectification term.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certified Copies and Legalization of Corporate Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección Mercantil (certified copy issuance and book protocolization).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After inscription, request the certified copy (copia certificada) of the registered instrument for use in bank onboarding and licensing procedures. Submit the corporate books (share register, minutes of shareholders, and minutes of directors) for protocolization and stamping by the Public Registry so that they become admissible evidence for corporate acts.
required_dossiers: Inscription reference or folio number of the S.A.
Application for certified copy (solicitud de copia certificada)
Blank corporate books: Registro de Accionistas, Libro de Actas de Junta Directiva, Libro de Actas de Asamblea de Accionistas
Payment receipt for book protocolization fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify binding, foliation, or signature defects upon the registry's observations; re-submit the corrected books with a covering letter and updated fee receipt.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with the DGI (RUC, Shareholder Information, and Electronic Invoicing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of Panama – Sede Electrónica or taxpayer service window (Ventanilla de Contribuyentes).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the RUC application (Form 001) online or at the DGI office, presenting the certified incorporation copies and the appointment of the legal representative. The DGI issues the RUC certificate and may request evidence of the fiscal domicile. File the shareholder information declaration and register for electronic invoicing (Factura Electrónica) because export and wholesale operations are anticipated.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the inscription at the Registro Público
Formulario RUC 001 and supplementary fiscal information form
Passport or ID and address of the legal representative
Certified copy of the bylaws and officers' appointment
Confirmation of fiscal domicile or bank reference
Shareholder information filing (Form 024 / SIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File all required supplementary declarations, appoint a fiscal agent to cure discrepancies, or re-present the full package at the taxpayer assistance window after correcting data inconsistencies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Aviso de Operación and MICI Industrial Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía Municipal del Distrito de Panamá – Tesorería Municipal; Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección General de Industrias y Empresas.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Aviso de Operación with the Municipality of the plant's district, attaching the RUC, property or lease title, and fire safety certificate; pay the corresponding municipal license fee. In parallel, register the establishment as an industrial enterprise with MICI's industrial registry and, if applicable, secure any export facilitation or incentive status for the manufacturing plant.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate
Formulario de Aviso de Operación signed by the legal representative
Title deed or lease agreement of the manufacturing site
Certificado de Seguridad Contra Incendios from the Cuerpo de Bomberos
MICI industrial registry application (Registro Industrial)
Plant layout plan showing floor dimensions and intended use
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Pay municipal interest or cure zoning inconsistencies by obtaining the Certificado de Uso from the Municipality; apply for administrative reconsideration with MICI if the industrial registration is denied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sectoral Licensing – MINSA Medical Device Registration, MiAMBIENTE Environmental Clearance, Bomberos and MITRADEL Occupational Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) – Dirección Nacional de Farmacia y Drogas; Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental; Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá; Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the establishment's Sanitary Operation Permit and the product's Registro Sanitario de Dispositivo Médico for the Color Doppler Ultrasound Console (Class II medical device under the Central American Technical Regulation adopted by MINSA), supported by CE/FDA evidence and ISO 13485 QMS documentation. File the environmental screening document or environmental impact study with MiAMBIENTE, execute the monitoring commitments, and pay the applicable environmental fee. Obtain the Bomberos occupancy and fire-safety certificate, and establish the MITRADEL-registered joint safety and health committee and worker training program. All clearances must be current before manufacturing commences.
required_dossiers: Registro Sanitario application with technical dossier of the ultrasound console
Declaration of Conformity (CE-MDR), FDA 510(k), or analogous evidence of prior registration
ISO 13485 certificate, ISO 14971 risk management file, and IEC 60601-1 / IEC 60601-2-37 test reports
Sanitary Operation Permit application and physical plant inspection checklist
MiAMBIENTE environmental screening form or environmental impact assessment with fee receipt
Bomberos fire-safety certificate and inspection act
MITRADEL employer registration form (Planilla de Empresa) and occupational safety program
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to MINSA technical observations by submitting supplementary safety and EMC test data or a revised classification argument; appeal MiAMBIENTE conditions before the Superior Environmental Tribunal; schedule Bomberos re-inspection after correcting fire-protection deficiencies; remedy MITRADEL objections by revising the occupational health plan.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección General de Industrias y Empresas; Alcaldía Municipal del Distrito de Panamá – Tesorería Municipal; Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) – Dirección Nacional de Farmacia y Drogas.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación Industrial (Municipal), Certificado de Registro Industrial (MICI), Permiso Sanitario de Operación de Establecimiento de Dispositivos Médicos (MINSA), and Registro Sanitario de Dispositivo Médico for the Color Doppler Ultrasound Console.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II – Diagnóstico Ambiental (Environmental Screening) under Executive Decree No. 123 of 2009; a full Environmental Impact Study (Category I EsIA) is not required for the ultrasound console assembly plant unless hazardous waste volumes or discharges exceed the regulatory thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Industrial liquid effluents must comply with MiAMBIENTE CETES parameters for discharge to municipal sewers or receiving waters (pH 6-9, BOD5, COD, TSS, oils and greases within published thresholds); VOC and particulate emissions are controlled under Ley No. 26 de 1998 and its implementing resolutions; hazardous waste, including electronic circuit board scrap and soldering residues, must be managed by authorized handlers under Ley No. 41 de 1998 and Basel Convention transboundary movement controls.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Certificado de Seguridad Contra Incendios issued by the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá in accordance with NFPA 101 / NFPA 1; structural load clearance for the production floor signed by a licensed Panamanian engineer; workplace registration with MITRADEL and the mandatory joint health and safety committee where the workforce exceeds 50 employees, together with the annual occupational risk assessment and employee medical surveillance program.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) — Sede Electrónica: https://sedeelectronica.dgi.gob.pa; customs administration: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) — SICE portal: https://www.ana.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: STEP 1: Incorporate the Sociedad Anónima (S.A.) through a licensed Panamanian law firm and inscribe the deed at the Registro Público de Panamá (no minimum capital; bearer shares abolished). STEP 2: Obtain the Aviso de Operación (municipal business license) for the registered office. STEP 3: Apply for the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) before the DGI via Sede Electrónica, attaching the public deed, Registro Público certificate, Aviso de Operación, passport or cédula of the legal representative, and the resident-agent certificate; the unified RUC serves for ISR, ITBMS, and withholding obligations. STEP 4: Register as exporter with ANA in the SICE system to obtain the export code. STEP 5: Enroll in the DGI electronic invoicing scheme and obtain the authorized invoice series. No minimum capital and no local ownership requirement apply; a resident agent and a fiscal representative must be continuously maintained.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity classification: the S.A. is mandatorily a taxable corporation (25% corporate ISR on Panama-source income) and cannot be disregarded or treated as a pass-through; Panama has no check-the-box rule and does not recognize foreign entity-election outcomes for treaty purposes. Available elections relevant to the exporter: (i) simplified small-taxpayer ISR/ITBMS gross-receipts regime where annual gross revenue is below the DGI ceiling; (ii) monthly versus quarterly ITBMS filing cycles according to DGI taxpayer categorization; (iii) election to offset excess ITBMS export input credits against other tax liabilities or to claim an annual cash refund (reintegro) from the DGI.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) — a VAT/GST-type transfer tax levied on supplies of movable goods and services in Panamanian territory, with destination-principle 0% rating for exports.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary registration threshold: any person habitually engaged in the sale of movable goods or taxable services in Panama must register for ITBMS (RUC) from the first taxable transaction. The B/.36,000 annual gross-revenue ceiling is relevant only for qualifying to the optional simplified small-taxpayer reporting regime, not for triggering or exempting registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Yes — mandatory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica en Línea) under Law 60 of 2019, Executive Decree 103 of 2021, and DGI resolutions, phased by taxpayer class: large taxpayers from July 2022, medium taxpayers from 2023, remaining small taxpayers from 2024. Every invoice (taxable, exempt, or zero-rated) must be generated in a DGI-authorized system and transmitted in real time in XML/JSON to the DGI; the DGI validates and returns a unique Número de Autorización, and the final invoice must carry the authorized alphanumeric series, a DGI QR (2D) code, and, for zero-rated exports, the ANA SICE export-declaration number. Corporate issuers must integrate through a certified API gateway or the DGI online portal; offline contingency issuance is restricted to DGI-approved system-outage procedures.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% ITBMS applies to: (i) exports of tangible goods (e.g., color Doppler ultrasound consoles under HS 9018.12) sold to a non-resident purchaser and physically removed from Panamanian customs territory, evidenced by an ANA SICE export declaration; and (ii) services rendered to non-residents for use and economic enjoyment entirely outside Panama, paid from abroad. The transaction remains within the ITBMS system at 0% (not exempt), preserving the exporter's right to recover the 7% ITBMS borne on imported raw materials, components, and local inputs via monthly offset or an annual refund (reintegro) from the DGI. The exporter must maintain audit-compliant inventory and sales records proving the goods' origin and export custody.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) filed electronically through the ANA SICE system
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical shipment from Panamanian territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (certificado de remesa) issued by the Panamanian bank evidencing receipt of the export proceeds in USD/Balboa
Commercial invoice referencing the applicable HS code (9018.12) and the SICE declaration number
Non-resident purchase order or export contract evidencing the foreign buyer and payment terms
Certificate of origin where preferential tariff treatment is claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI electronically cross-checks every zero-rated supply against ANA exit records, banking remittance certificates, and the purchaser's non-resident status. Failure to evidence the receipt of export funds within the standard 180-day repatriation/corroboration window or any documentary deficiency triggers recharacterization as a domestic supply, assessment of 7% ITBMS on the FOB value plus monthly statutory interest, and retrospective clawback within the general three-year statute of review, extended to six years for incomplete, inaccurate, or fraudulent declarations. Administrative fines of up to 100% of the tax and up to B/.10,000 per irregularly issued invoice may be imposed; criminal liability for fiscal defraudation carries 2-5 years' imprisonment, and customs smuggling fines reach up to 300% of the merchandise value. Directors, the legal representative, and the registered agent may be held jointly and severally liable when false export documentation is presented.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Tasa Única Anual) — flat corporate renewal fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance of Panama; collected through the DGI e-tax portal or Banco Nacional de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fixed annual deadline of July 15 of each calendar year; unpaid amounts may still be settled via the DGI portal with surcharges through the October 15 reset date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: B/.50 late surcharge if paid after July 15; additional B/.100 surcharge if still unpaid after October 15; five consecutive years of non-payment triggers administrative strike-off (cancellation) by the Registro Público, with reinstatement conditional on payment of all arrears plus a B/.150 restoration fee

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporation Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI (Dirección General de Ingresos) — electronic filing through the DGI e-tax declaration system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before April 30 for fiscal years ending December 31; DGI may phase taxpayers through an annual e-filing calendar, with the April 30 date as the general long-stop for calendar-year entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge of 10% of the tax assessed plus 1% monthly compounded interest; failure to file exposes the corporation to fines between B/.100 and B/.5,000 and suspension of the DGI tax-clearance certificate (Paz y Salvo)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Sworn Shareholder List Declaration (Declaración Jurada de Accionistas) under DGI Resolution No. 201-1529 of 2019
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI (Dirección General de Ingresos) — electronic submission in the shareholders information module
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 60 calendar days following the mandatory annual general meeting of shareholders; for calendar-year corporations the DGI administrative calendar sets a long-stop filing date of November 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing blocks issuance of the Paz y Salvo and prevents the Registro Público from registering share transfers and director changes; monetary penalties up to B/.5,000 may be assessed under Resolution 201-1529

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Sworn Declaration of Final Beneficial Owners (Declaración de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI — Registry of Final Beneficial Owners (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales, Law 23 of 2015 and implementing resolutions)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing due by March 31 following the fiscal year end; separate update within 30 days of any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership; new incorporations must file within 30 days of registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or maintain updated UBO data subjects the entity to fines up to B/.5,000; authorities may also suspend certain corporate acts, such as distributions or share transfers, until the beneficial ownership register is regularized

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Shareholders and Ratification of Corporate Minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records maintained by the licensed Resident Agent (agente residente); minutes recorded and bound in the corporate Minute Book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Mandatory at least once each corporate year and no later than 15 months after the preceding annual general meeting; commonly scheduled on the registration anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Absence of timely annual minutes impairs the shareholder declaration timeline and complicates share transfer filings; third-party transactions requiring board or shareholder authority may be challenged if corporate authority is not evidenced in the minutes

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Resident Agent Continuation and Registered Office Maintenance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Resident Agent (agente residente) in Panama; continuation docs retained by agent and available to the Registro Público
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On each annual anniversary of incorporation or at the commencement of each agent contract year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Resignation of the resident agent without replacement triggers DGI and Registro Público delinquency warnings and eventually administrative strike-off; the corporation loses legal standing to contract or litigate in Panama until a new resident agent is appointed

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies if any of the following conditions are met: (1) the corporation is a listed issuer supervised by the Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores (SMV); (2) it is a bank, insurer, fiduciary, or other financial-services provider regulated by the Superintendencia de Banca (SBP) or the Superintendencia de Seguros (SSM); (3) its gross Panama-source annual income exceeds B/.300,000, in which case DGI requires audited financial statements to accompany the annual income tax return. A fully inactive offshore S.A. with no Panama-source activity carries no statutory audit obligation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Panama for public-interest entities; IFRS for SMEs (or other consistent local GAAP accepted by DGI) for private non-listed S.As.; financial reporting in Panamanian balboa (PAB), pegged 1:1 to USD

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The S.A. must keep a physical shareholders register (Libro de Registro de Acciones) that is updated at every share transfer. Under Law 23 of 2015, a final beneficial owner (UBO) ledger is maintained by the resident agent identifying each beneficial owner, ID or passport number, and percentage of shareholding. At the mandatory annual general meeting, shareholders ratify the register, after which the DGI shareholder declaration (Resolution 201-1529) must be filed within 60 days, and the DGI UBO declaration by March 31. Any transfer that shifts beneficial ownership must be recorded in the share register and reported to DGI within 30 days; bearer share coupons, where still authorized, must be immobilized and held by a licensed custodian or trustee.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Acciones)
Register of Directors (Libro de Actas y Resoluciones del Directorio)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de la Asamblea General de Accionistas)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $250-$800 per year, depending on provider, availability of nominee officers, and priority corporate services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $3,000-$8,500 per year when the B/.300,000 gross-revenue threshold or a regulator requires an independent audit; nil for a fully inactive offshore S.A.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% Impuesto sobre la Renta (ISR) on net taxable income; a 2% presumptive minimum income tax (Rentas Presuntas) applies when the standard computation yields less than the imputed floor.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial scope: only Panama-source income is taxed; export sales of portable color Doppler ultrasound consoles to foreign buyers - where title, risk, and beneficial use pass outside Panama - are treated as exempt foreign-source income. Free Zone and Panama Pacifico operators enjoy 0%-5% ISR on qualifying export profits; Multinational Headquarters (SEM) licensees can reach 0% on qualifying offshore income. Sectoral investment incentive laws may provide tax credits for manufacturing and re-equipment, but such credits require prior DGI approval and strict documentary support.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 745 (Declaracion Jurada Anual de Renta); filed electronically via the DGI portal: e-Tax / TAT (Transmision Automatica de Transferencia de Datos).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; interim compliance includes quarterly advance payments (anticipos) and monthly ITBMS returns where the entity has Panamanian registrations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end (standard calendar year: January 1 - December 31). The DGI annual calendar staggers the due date in February-March of the following year by the last digit of the RUC, with March 31 as the maximum statutory end-date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All income accrued from Panama-source activities, including intra-group sales, services, and royalties economically attributable to Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident S.A. without local trade: enter zero and attach a sworn statement describing the foreign-source nature of export sales; keep bills of lading, letters of credit, and purchase orders evidencing offshore title transfer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses directly attributable to taxable Panama-source income: COGS, freight, customs duties, local overhead, depreciation, and transfer-pricing-compliant related-party charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only deductions supported by documentary flow and economically linked to Panama-source revenue; cap related-party recharges at arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income minus allowable deductions; subject to the 25% headline rate and the presumptive minimum tax floor.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If zero or negative, reconcile the loss carryforward (maximum 5 years) on the attached schedule; substantiate any transfer-pricing adjustment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: ISR at 25% of net taxable income or 2% presumptive minimum tax on the imputed base, whichever is higher.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute ISR only on Panama-source net income; export proceeds routed through offshore accounts remain outside the tax base only when the economic substance of the sale is foreign.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance payments (anticipos), third-party withholdings, and tax credits applied against the tax determined.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Offset only Panamanian withholdings (e.g., 2% on local service fees) and properly documented SEM/free-zone credits; refund requests trigger a DGI audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the 5% dividend withholding tax on dividends declared out of taxed earnings or the 10% rate on distributions from non-taxed earnings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The S.A. acts as withholding agent for the non-resident shareholder; declare distributions on Form 745 even when the dividend is wired offshore.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: surcharge of 5% per month or fraction up to 25% of the tax due, plus late-payment interest of 1% per month; formal-infraction fines for non-filing range B/.50 - B/.5,000; persistent default triggers DGI collection procedures, bank garnishment, and suspension of the corporate registration.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% for dividends paid out of profits already taxed at the corporate level (both resident and non-resident shareholders); 10% when the distribution originates from profits not subject to Panamanian ISR (e.g., exempt foreign-source income or free-zone preferential income). The tax is definitive and levied on the gross dividend, with no additional non-resident surcharge.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama's DTA network (Barbados, Czech Republic, France, Ireland, Italy, Korea, Mexico, Netherlands, Portugal, Qatar, Singapore, Spain, UAE, United Kingdom) may reduce the dividend WHT to 5%-10%. Protocol: (1) obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the treaty-state competent authority; (2) present the TRC, beneficial-ownership statement, and treaty self-assessment to the Panamanian paying S.A. before or at distribution; (3) retain the documents for DGI inspection. Relief operates at the source without prior DGI authorization but is subject to subsequent audit; the withholding agent must justify the reduced rate in the annual reconciliation.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to non-domiciled IP holders: 12.5% statutory; DTA-reduced rates commonly 0%-10%. Debt interest paid to foreign creditors: 5% statutory; DTA rates typically 5%. Royalties on medical-imaging software, algorithms, and patents licensed to Panama-registered entities must be supported by a registered license agreement and an arm's-length valuation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/.1,000,000 (USD 1,000,000 equivalent): annual aggregate related-party transactions exceeding this threshold trigger the mandatory TP Informative Return (Formulario 735) and preparation of a Local File study; Master File obligations attach for groups exceeding the Decree 475/2013 group-revenue thresholds (B/.250 million group consolidated revenue).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's territorial system does not impose a universal ESR regime like UAE or Bermuda, but substance is enforced measurably: SEM licensees and Free Zone/ Panama Pacifico operators must satisfy minimum local payroll and operating-expenditure ratios; DGI's GAAR (Law 254/2021) permits recharacterization or denial of tax-residence certificates where the S.A. lacks premises, personnel, and decision-making functions; the Beneficial Ownership Registry (Law 23/2015, UAF) requires accurate ultimate-owner disclosure. A medical-device export S.A. functioning as a pure invoicing conduit - without books, office, or management in Panama - is treated as a tax-haven shell and loses treaty and territorial protections.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission or falsification of Panama-source income; submitting a zero or false Form 745 while generating taxable local revenue; fabricated export contracts and sham invoices to shift profits offshore.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of up to 300% of the evaded tax and imprisonment of 2-5 years, increased to 4-10 years where the evasion is aggravated by use of offshore accounts, false documents, or a shell nominee structure; revocation of regime benefits and 25% tax re-determination plus surcharges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives who certify false returns face personal criminal exposure, civil restitution for the unpaid tax, precautionary seizure of personal and corporate assets, and travel bans pending criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse / Dormant S.A. Non-Compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the S.A. indefinitely without filing annual returns, paying the annual corporate stamp tax, registering beneficial owners, or demonstrating any operational substance while commercial activity continues.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monetary fines per the Fiscal Code for each unfiled obligation (B/.50 - B/.5,000 per infraction), plus the 5%-monthly late-filing surcharge; the Corporate Registry may suspend or cancel the S.A.'s legal status, triggering asset illiquidity and contract nullity; economic recharacterization under GAAR at 25% plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the entity's tax debts when they directed the inactivity; continued operation under a suspended entity exposes directors personally in civil proceedings, and the tax court may impose a travel restriction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) declaration with the UAF; omission of required due diligence on Swift LC / TT wire payors and end-buyers; payment routing through undisclosed intermediaries with unexplained commissions in medical-device consignments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to B/.1,000,000 and suspension of licenses under Law 23/2015; money-laundering offenses under the Penal Code carry imprisonment of 5-10 years and confiscation of assets; DGI may treat unexplained commissions as non-deductible distributions subject to 10% dividend tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Individual officers who authorized the transaction are criminally prosecutable; risk of UAF asset freezes, personal travel bans, and disqualification from managing Panamanian companies.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Related-party transactions exceeding B/.1,000,000 with no Form 735 filing or TP study; intercompany pricing above or below arm's length to erode the Panamanian taxable base; undocumented royalty or interest flows from the local distribution entity to the foreign parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI transfer-pricing adjustment and re-computation of taxable income at 25%; penalty surcharge of up to 25% on the adjusted tax; mandatory compliance fines of B/.5,000 - B/.50,000 for omitted documentation; interest at 1% monthly.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative who signs the informative return or approved intercompany contracts may be held personally liable for the penalty portion under the tax-procedure liability rule and may face a director ban in egregious cases of document falsification.
